feedback.problem:
Let $(x,y)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $x+y?$

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+3y=15 \\ 0.6x-0.8y=1\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the second equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+3y=15 &  \\ 0.6x-0.8y=1 & |\,\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}4x+3y=15 \\ 6x-8y=10\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second equation by $-2,$ we will get a $12x$ term in the first equation that can cancel with the $-12x$ term in the second equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+3y=15 & |\,\times 3 \\ 6x-8y=10 & |\,\times -2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}12x+9y=45 \\ -12x+16y=-20\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{12x}+9y & =45 \\ -\cancel{12x}+16y & =-20 \\ (9y+16y) & =(45-20) \\ 25y & =25 \\ y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $y=1$ into the equation $4x+3y=15$ to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+3y & =15 \\ 4x+3 & =15 \\ 4x & =15-3 \\ 4x & =12 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=3$ and $y=1.$ So, 

$$
x+y=3+1=4.
$$
